quotes.text: " Tom did play hookey, and he had a very good time. He got back home barely in season to help Jim, the small colored boy, saw next-day's wood and split the kindlings before supper-- at least he was there in time to tell his adventures to Jim while Jim did three-fourths of the work. Tom's younger brother (or rather half-brother) Sid was already through with his part of the work (picking up chips), for he was a quiet boy, and had no adventurous, troublesome ways. While Tom was eating his supper, and stealing sugar as opportunity offered, Aunt Polly asked him questions that were full of guile, and very deep-- for she wanted to trap him into damaging revealments. Like many other simple-hearted souls, it was her pet vanity to believe she was endowed with a talent for dark and mysterious diplomacy, and she loved to contemplate her most transparent devices as marvels of low cunning. Said she: "Tom, it was middling warm in school, warn't it?"

quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What's that you got?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Dead cat."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Lemme see him, Huck. My, he's pretty stiff. Where'd you get him?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Bought him off'n a boy."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What did you give?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I give a blue ticket and a bladder that I got at the slaughter-house."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Where'd you get the blue ticket?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Bought it off'n Ben Rogers two weeks ago for a hoop-stick."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Say-- what is dead cats good for, Huck?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Good for? Cure warts with."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No! Is that so? I know something that's better."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I bet you don't. What is it?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Why, spunk-water."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Spunk-water! I wouldn't give a dern for spunk-water."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You wouldn't, wouldn't you? D'you ever try it?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No, I hain't. But Bob Tanner did."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Who told you so!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Why, he told Jeff Thatcher, and Jeff told Johnny Baker, and Johnny told Jim Hollis, and Jim told Ben Rogers, and Ben told a nigger, and the nigger told me. There now!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Well, what of it? They'll all lie. Leastways all but the nigger. I don't know HIM. But I never see a nigger that WOULDN'T lie. Shucks! Now you tell me how Bob Tanner done it, Huck."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Why, he took and dipped his hand in a rotten stump where the rain-water was."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "In the daytime?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Certainly."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "With his face to the stump?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes. Least I reckon so."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Did he say anything?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I don't reckon he did. I don't know."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Aha! Talk about trying to cure warts with spunk-water such a blame fool way as that! Why, that ain't a-going to do any good. You got to go all by yourself, to the middle of the woods, where you know there's a spunk-water stump, and just as it's midnight you back up against the stump and jam your hand in and say: 'Barley-corn, barley-corn, injun-meal shorts, Spunk-water, spunk-water, swaller these warts,' and then walk away quick, eleven steps, with your eyes shut, and then turn around three times and walk home without speaking to anybody.  Because if you speak the charm's busted."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Well, that sounds like a good way; but that ain't the way Bob Tanner done."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No, sir, you can bet he didn't, becuz he's the wartiest boy in this town; and he wouldn't have a wart on him if he'd knowed how to work spunk-water. I've took off thousands of warts off of my hands that way, Huck. I play with frogs so much that I've always got considerable many warts. Sometimes I take 'em off with a bean."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes, bean's good. I've done that."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Have you? What's your way?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You take and split the bean, and cut the wart so as to get some blood, and then you put the blood on one piece of the bean and take and dig a hole and bury it 'bout midnight at the crossroads in the dark of the moon, and then you burn up the rest of the bean. You see that piece that's got the blood on it will keep drawing and drawing, trying to fetch the other piece to it, and so that helps the blood to draw the wart, and pretty soon off she comes."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes, that's it, Huck-- that's it; though when you're burying it if you say 'Down bean; off wart; come no more to bother me!' it's better. That's the way Joe Harper does, and he's been nearly to Coonville and most everywheres. But say-- how do you cure 'em with dead cats?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Why, you take your cat and go and get in the graveyard 'long about midnight when somebody that was wicked has been buried; and when it's midnight a devil will come, or maybe two or three, but you can't see 'em, you can only hear something like the wind, or maybe hear 'em talk; and when they're taking that feller away, you heave your cat after 'em and say, 'Devil follow corpse, cat follow devil, warts follow cat, I'm done with ye!' That'll fetch ANY wart."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Sounds right. D'you ever try it, Huck?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No, but old Mother Hopkins told me."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Well, I reckon it's so, then. Becuz they say she's a witch."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Say! Why, Tom, I KNOW she is. She witched pap. Pap says so his own self. He come along one day, and he see she was a-witching him, so he took up a rock, and if she hadn't dodged, he'd a got her. Well, that very night he rolled off'n a shed wher' he was a layin drunk, and broke his arm."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Why, that's awful. How did he know she was a-witching him?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Lord, pap can tell, easy. Pap says when they keep looking at you right stiddy, they're a-witching you. Specially if they mumble. Becuz when they mumble they're saying the Lord's Prayer backards."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Say, Hucky, when you going to try the cat?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "To-night. I reckon they'll come after old Hoss Williams to-night."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "But they buried him Saturday. Didn't they get him Saturday night?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Why, how you talk! How could their charms work till midnight?-- and THEN it's Sunday. Devils don't slosh around much of a Sunday, I don't reckon."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I never thought of that. That's so. Lemme go with you?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Of course-- if you ain't afeard."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Afeard! 'Tain't likely. Will you meow?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes-- and you meow back, if you get a chance. Last time, you kep' me a-meowing around till old Hays went to throwing rocks at me and says 'Dern that cat!' and so I hove a brick through his window-- but don't you tell."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I won't. I couldn't meow that night, becuz auntie was watching me, but I'll meow this time. Say-- what's that?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Nothing but a tick."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Where'd you get him?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Out in the woods."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What'll you take for him?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I don't know. I don't want to sell him."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "All right. It's a mighty small tick, anyway."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, anybody can run a tick down that don't belong to them. I'm satisfied with it. It's a good enough tick for me."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Sho, there's ticks a plenty. I could have a thousand of 'em if I wanted to."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Well, why don't you? Becuz you know mighty well you can't. This is a pretty early tick, I reckon. It's the first one I've seen this year."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Say, Huck-- I'll give you my tooth for him."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Less see it."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Is it genuwyne?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Well, all right,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "it's a trade."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Thomas Sawyer!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Sir!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Come up here. Now, sir, why are you late again, as usual?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I STOPPED TO TALK WITH HUCKLEBERRY FINN!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You-- you did what?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Stopped to talk with Huckleberry Finn."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Thomas Sawyer, this is the most astounding confession I have ever listened to. No mere ferule will answer for this offence. Take off your jacket."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Now, sir, go and sit with the girls! And let this be a warning to you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "made a mouth"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Please take it -- I got more."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Let me see it."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It's nice-- make a man."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It's a beautiful man-- now make me coming along."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It's ever so nice -- I wish I could draw."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It's easy,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I'll learn you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, will you? When?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "At noon. Do you go home to dinner?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I'll stay if you will."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Good-- that's a whack. What's your name?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Becky Thatcher. What's yours? Oh, I know. It's Thomas Sawyer."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "That's the name they lick me by. I'm Tom when I'm good. You call me Tom, will you?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, it ain't anything."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes it is."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No it ain't. You don't want to see."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes I do, indeed I do. Please let me."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You'll tell."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No I won't-- deed and deed and double deed won't."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You won't tell anybody at all? Ever, as long as you live?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No, I won't ever tell ANYbody. Now let me."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, YOU don't want to see!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Now that you treat me so, I WILL see."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I LOVE YOU."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, you bad thing!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "turned down,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown
